The story of the lighthouse, as it continues, finds itself woven into the fabric of the local memory. The tower, though unlit, remains a silent sentinel against the changing tides. The iron gallery, once a lace of holes, now feels like a map of time itself. The shadow that stretches across the water on a clear evening is no longer just a physical phenomenon; it becomes a metaphor for the passage of time. As the sun dips lower, the shadow seems to lengthen, pulling the image of the tower further into the distance, as if the structure itself is stretching to keep pace with the day.

The keeper's cottage, though long unused, stands as a testament to the quiet life that once lived there. The grey stone, the slate roof, the deep windows — each detail reminds one of the care taken in building such a place. The tin of tea on the shelf is a small but significant detail, a reminder of the simple acts of daily life that have been forgotten. The stove, cold and capped, speaks of the long winters that have passed without the warmth of the keeper. Yet, the presence of the cottage is a constant, a small anchor in the vastness of the bay.
